methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit was designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This involved breaking down complex sentences into simpler, more manageable statements. For the original research topic, the focus was on extracting the core requirements of the LFSR, such as its size, tap positions, reset behavior, and maximal-length property. For the generated technical specification, the decomposition focused on the combinational logic function, enhanced combinational description, interface behavior, timing dependencies, and register updates.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Taps are at bit positions 5 and 3
Bit positions are counted from right to left, starting from 1
LFSR should cycle through 2^5 - 1 = 31 states before repeating
The all-zero state should be avoided
Reset should reset the LFSR output such that all bits are set to 1 (q[4:0] = 5'b11111)
module top_module( input clk, input reset, output reg [4:0] q);
spec_atomic_units: module top_module( input clk, input reset, output reg [4:0] q);
Combinational logic generates the next state of the 5-bit Galois LFSR
When reset is asserted, all bits of the output q are set to 1
LFSR has taps at positions 5 and 3
Output q changes on the rising edge of clk
When reset is high, q is synchronously set to 5'b11111 on the next rising edge of clk
When reset is low, q changes to the next state of the LFSR on each rising edge of clk
The circuit contains a 5-bit register q
